name: Motors and variable speed drives
principle: Three-phase induction motors remain the workhorse driver; synchronous machines serve large compressors and high-efficiency duties. Efficiency classes IE1 to IE5 are defined in IEC 60034-30-1 for line-operated motors. Variable frequency drives rectify the supply and synthesise an adjustable-voltage, adjustable-frequency output, giving soft starts, process speed control, energy savings on centrifugal loads (affinity laws: power roughly follows speed cubed) and regenerative braking on hoisting duties. Drives inject harmonics, so input filters or multi-pulse/active front ends are applied.

process_steps.name: Drive rectifier converts AC supply to DC bus
Motor converts electrical to mechanical power
Closed-loop control (V/f, flux vector) tracks torque and speed references

limitations: long cable runs to MV motors need reflected-wave management and surge protection
harmonic distortion and bearing currents are managed by filters and insulated bearings
advantages: cube-law energy savings on centrifugal loads
replaces control valves and dampers with speed control, cutting throttling losses
